title: Mesh-window cutover calendar for staggered model, console & API rollouts
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Goal: Define and ship a machine-readable cutover calendar ("mesh windows") and operational guardrails that let runtime, console, and API teams coordinate staggered rollouts with predictable capacity and clear rollback semantics.

Scope: calendar format + automation signals, weekend safehold rules, capacity sentinel integration with capacity-dashboard, clear canary phasing per surface, owner/roster mapping, and an exportable 'calendar-as-code' manifest used by the launch conductor. Not in scope: per-model scoring policies and traffic-split implementation (handled by runtime team separately).

Why: Recent cross-surface releases revealed contention between model rollouts (high GPU demand) and console feature launches that spike API traffic. The mesh-window concept groups related launches into coordinated, non-overlapping windows and adds a sentinel that gates launches based on capacity and SLO health. That reduces simultaneous peak risk and gives ops a predictable signal for emergency safehold.

Design decisions and trade-offs considered:
- Mesh windows are weekly 4-hour primary windows + 2-hour bleed for rollback; chosen to balance developer velocity and ops overhead. Shorter windows increase coordination overhead; longer windows slow downstream features.
- Calendar-as-code (YAML manifest) chosen for automation and auditability. We accept an initial manual review step before enabling auto-approve to reduce blast radius.
- Capacity sentinel thresholds default to 70% GPU util and 5% P99 latency uplift over baseline. These are conservative and can be tuned after two pilot releases.
- Canary phasing: runtime model canaries will be aligned to API and console canaries by cohort keys to measure surface-level regressions. This requires an instrumentation contract with infra and SDK teams.

Acceptance criteria:
- Machine-readable manifest template committed to repo (confluence + GH link below).
- Launch conductor picks up the calendar and emits preflight signals to teams (capacity, canary, blackouts).
- Week-of-run playbook (owner roster, ops runbooks, rollback checklist) reviewed and signed off by runtime, console, API leads.
- Two pilot rollouts run (one runtime-only, one cross-surface) with no SLO-impacting incidents.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: teams bypass calendar and schedule urgent launches -> Mitigation: make calendar integration the default in the release gating checklist and add a temporary policy that flags non-calendar releases in weekly release review.
- Risk: sentinel false positives block important deploys -> Mitigation: allow manual override with documented escalations and a 15-minute guarded approval window.
- Risk: capacity metrics lag or are noisy -> Mitigation: use rolling 5-min window with anomaly smoothing and require two independent signals before block.

Next steps (owner):
- 2025-02-18: Draft YAML schema for mesh-window manifest (Derek Stone) -> DONE, PR open.
- 2025-02-20: Converge on sentinel thresholds with Infra (Aisha Kumar + Mei Tan) -> decision: 70% util / 5% P99 uplift provisional.
- 2025-02-25: Build minimal launch-conductor hook to read calendar and emit preflight check events (ENG-4921) -> In progress (ENG).
- 2025-03-03: Run first pilot (runtime model v2 classifier) in a mesh window -> Planned.
- 2025-03-10: Cross-surface pilot (console feature + model tweak) and postmortem -> Planned.

Notes on coordination and comms:
- Weekly synchronization cadence: Monday 10:00AM cross-surface triage to lock the week’s mesh windows. Owners must update calendar-as-code before the meeting.
- On-call & cutover roster: include primary + secondary for each surface, email and Slack escalation playbook included in runbook.
- Documentation artifacts: brief Confluence runbook, calendar YAML example, and a 'how-to' quickstart for engineers to add their launch to the mesh.

Links and artifacts:
- Confluence runbook (draft): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PM/pages/mesh-windows-cutover-runbook
- GH PR (calendar schema): https://github.com/redwood-inference/release-tools/pull/214
- Capacity dashboard prototype: https://internal.redwood.tools/dashboards/capacity-sentinel
- Pilot checklist doc (Drive): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1abcPilotChecklist

Post-release review criteria:
- Postmortem must capture latency/cost delta per release window and any manual overrides.
- If sentinel blocked release and manual override was used, record rationale and adjust thresholds or incident flow.
- Add instrumentation gaps to the backlog if any visibility issues were discovered.
acceptance_criteria: YAML calendar manifest committed to release-tools repo
Conductor emits preflight signals and prevents non-calendar rollouts
Week-of-run playbook signed by runtime, console, API leads
Two pilot rollouts executed without SLO-impacting incidents
